result.summary: Skip automatic Tor onion service creation when explicit `-bind` parameters are configured without a dedicated `=onion` bind, while keeping the Tor controller active for outbound SOCKS proxy discovery. Reject wildcard onion binds at startup when `-listenonion` is enabled, and defer starting Tor control until P2P listeners have bound successfully.
result.problem: When explicit `-bind` arguments are supplied without a dedicated onion listener, automatic Tor service setup forwards incoming Tor connections to a standard P2P listener. The node cannot distinguish Tor connections arriving on this port from standard clearnet or localhost traffic, causing them to be misclassified and potentially granted IP-based whitelist permissions (such as `-whitelist=127.0.0.1`).
evidence: PR description: "With a normal -bind (but no dedicated onion bind), automatic Tor services can forward incoming connections to the normal P2P listener, where they may be misclassified and inherit IP-based whitelist permissions."
Commit 448db280e3: "Start Tor control only after successful P2P binding so a failed bind cannot race service creation with a target owned by another process."
Issue #33458: "Documentation trap when using -bind in conjunction with (automatically configured) Tor hidden services".
result.scope_notes: Changes behavior for existing configurations that set `-bind` but omitted an explicit `=onion` bind: these nodes will stop advertising or accepting incoming Tor connections automatically until `-bind=<addr>:<port>=onion` is added.
result.changed_since_previous: No substantive architectural changes; rebased and updated documentation and functional tests.
result.card: Bitcoin Core skips automatic Tor onion service creation when nodes specify explicit -bind addresses without a dedicated -bind=<addr>=onion listener, warning the operator while keeping Tor control active for outbound proxy discovery. This prevents Tor traffic forwarded to shared P2P listeners from being misclassified and mistakenly inheriting IP-based whitelist permissions. In addition, wildcard onion binds are rejected at startup if automatic onion listening is enabled, and Tor controller startup is deferred until after socket binding succeeds so failed binds do not expose an unowned port.

risk.why: Mistakes in listener configuration or Tor controller handling could disable incoming onion connectivity or prevent the node from binding properly at startup.
